subject: Draft: AvalonLogix case study — redlines, metrics check and quote approval
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana@avalonlogix.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@avalonlogix.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: AvalonLogix case study — redlines, metrics check and quote approval

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for agreeing to collaborate on a short case study highlighting AvalonLogix's work with Redwood Inference. Attached is our second draft (Avalon_case_draft_v2.docx). We focused on the pilot outcomes and included a short customer quote in the final section; please treat that as placeholder until you confirm exact phrasing.

Could you do a quick fact-check on the performance numbers in section 2 (we have 42% inference cost reduction and median latency 140ms at p95) and let us know if those are accurate to publish? If the metrics look off, tell us what to replace them with. Also:
- Any redlines you want in the narrative copy?
- Approval or edit of the customer quote (below the case highlights) — we can adjust tone/length.
- Please confirm whether AvalonLogix legal needs a separate sign-off step (we can add a signature page).

If helpful, we can hop on a 20-min call this week to walk through changes.

Attachments: Avalon_case_draft_v2.docx

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference
(h) 415-555-0192 | hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

--
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM serving

From: Dana Lee <dana@avalonlogix.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@avalonlogix.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: AvalonLogix case study — redlines, metrics check and quote approval

Hannah —

Thanks for sending this over. Tom and I reviewed and added inline comments and a short PDF of our redlines (Avalon_comments_0908.pdf). High-level:
- The 42% cost reduction is correct but it should be called "inference unit cost" reduction and reference Q1–Q2 2026 pilot window.
- Latency numbers are slightly optimistic: p95 was ~160ms for the 2k token long-tail tests. We can approve publishing 160ms (p95) and note the test conditions in a parenthetical.
- We removed a sentence that implied Redwood handled model training — please remove that phrase (we trained with our in-house team).
- Quote: suggested tightening to one sentence — we propose: "Redwood's inference runtime cut our inference costs by over 40% while preserving response quality during peak loads." If that reads ok, we can sign off.

Legal asked to see a final PDF with the quote highlighted; they typically need an approval email from an executive. I can provide that once we get a final pass.

Attached: Avalon_comments_0908.pdf

Best,
Dana Lee
Director of Infrastructure
AvalonLogix
(d) 617-555-3377

Folks — forwarding AvalonLogix's redlines (attached). Key asks from Dana: adjust phrasing around training, change p95 latency to 160ms, and mark the 42% as "inference unit cost reduction (Q1–Q2 2026)". They want the quote shortened — suggested one-liner below.

Can you review and confirm: 
1) The latency/metrics wording is consistent with our telemetry (Markus — can you confirm the p95 result and recommended phrasing?)
2) The proposed quote change is acceptable from a marketing POV and length (Stephanie — any preference on tone?)
3) Any legal / IP concerns about naming specific internal tools — legal has asked if we referenced any non-public kernels. I haven't referenced product internals, but flag if you see any.

If we can get sign-off internally today, I'll send an updated PDF to Dana for exec approval.

Thanks,
Hannah

[Attachment: Avalon_comments_0908.pdf]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FWD: AvalonLogix comments — need copy/metrics confirmation and quote approval

Hannah / Stephanie —

Confirmed on the telemetry side: for the pilot window (Q1–Q2 2026), average inference unit cost dropped 42% on the benchmark workload we ran with their 8k context model; p95 latency from our logs for the longest test batches was ~158–165ms depending on batch alignment. Recommend we phrase as: "p95 latency ~160ms (long-tail batch tests)" and call out the pilot window.

Suggested marketing copy for the one-line quote: "Redwood's inference runtime reduced our per-inference cost by over 40% while keeping response consistency during peak loads."

Also: legal asked whether the phrase "model kernels optimized by Redwood" implies proprietary tech. I'd remove "kernels" and keep "runtime optimizations" if we need to mention implementation. Stephanie — if you prefer a more customer-forward tone I can rework the quote.

Markus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hannah —

This looks great, thanks for the quick turn. The wording Markus suggested reads well to us. We attached the signed approval (signed_case_permission.pdf) for the case study and a short note from legal confirming a single-exec approval is sufficient. The only tiny tweak: change "per-inference cost" to "inference unit cost" in the quote.

Final approved quote (approved by Dana Lee, Director of Infrastructure):
"Redwood's inference runtime reduced our inference unit cost by over 40% while keeping response consistency during peak loads."

Legal note: AvalonLogix legal will send a brief approval email to your legal team; expect a cc. Otherwise you have permission to publish once the final PDF is returned with our logo placement confirmed.

Thanks again — happy to be a reference.

Dana
